raw: 15.1 ELINT: Radar Signatures and Weapons Systems Emissions[^35]
teaching_note: ELINT concerns non-communications electromagnetic signals, while a measured feature set and an identification of a particular system are separate claims. Frequency, timing or amplitude patterns can overlap across emitters and depend on sensor calibration, sampling and observation geometry. A classroom label is a hypothesis about supplied synthetic measurements, not evidence of a real weapons system, operator or location; no reception or live collection is authorized.
title: ELINT: Radar Signatures and Weapons Systems Emissions

teaching_note: The inherited EMINT abbreviation and C4I label require an explicit source-specific definition; do not treat the broad criminal-investigations book listing as an authoritative technical taxonomy. Distinguish intentional emissions from unintended emanations and detection of energy from recoverable information. This source set does not establish recoverability, performance or a system-specific leakage claim, so those remain unknown rather than inviting interception or reconstruction.
title: EMINT: C4I System Emanations

raw: 15.3 Tempest and Van Eck Radiation: Standards and Countermeasures
teaching_note: TEMPEST is associated with compromising-emanations protection, whereas 'Van Eck' names a class of historical emanation demonstrations; neither term establishes that a particular device leaks usable content. The inherited ATLAS and software-assurance references do not specify applicable emanation limits, certification procedures or tested countermeasure performance. Keep this a conceptual distinction: current thresholds and efficacy remain unsupported, and there is no signal capture, content reconstruction or bypass exercise.
title: Tempest and Van Eck Radiation: Standards and Countermeasures

teaching_note: SDR moves some radio-processing functions into software; it does not remove the limits of hardware bandwidth, calibration or sampling. In a completed synthetic table, bins 1–4 contain powers [2, 2, 8, 2] arbitrary units and a supplied comparison rule flags values above 5; the transformation flags bin 3 only. A calibration row adds a +6-unit instrument offset to bin 3, so offset correction yields [2, 2, 2, 2] and withdraws the apparent anomaly; without that row the cause is unknown, not an identified emitter. Duplicating the same table is no corroboration, and removing calibration stops attribution; the attached software-assurance sources do not validate SDR performance, and all work is arithmetic on fictional records, without hardware, reception or transmission.
title: Software-Defined Radio (SDR) for Intelligence Applications

teaching_note: An RF map represents measurements at sampled positions and times under declared equipment settings; interpolation is a derived estimate, not an observation at every pixel. Missing samples, multipath and instrument bias can produce a pattern without locating an emitter, and repetition with one miscalibrated instrument need not supply independent confirmation. In a fictional grid, cells A/B have values 2/8 but B alone lacks a calibration record and was recorded in a different environment, so a spatial comparison stops at 'not comparable' rather than an emitter claim. The NGA mission page and analytic standards do not establish propagation parameters or geolocation accuracy; no real services, reception, decoding or persons are mapped.
title: RF Mapping and Spectrum Intelligence
